definition: Hyperband is a resource-allocation and successive-halving strategy for rapidly discarding weak configurations. BOHB combines this multi-fidelity racing idea with a model-based sampler so promising regions of the hyperparameter space receive more trials.
intuition: Run many cheap candidates, repeatedly halve the pool, and give more resources to survivors; BOHB biases new candidates toward regions that already look good.
mathematical_foundation:
$$
n_{j+1} = \left\lfloor n_j / \eta \right\rfloor, \qquad r_{j+1} = \eta r_j
$$

Successive halving keeps roughly the best `1/\eta` fraction while increasing their resource. BOHB supplies model-based candidates to the brackets.
advantages: Allocates more budget to promising trials and stops weak trials early.
Works well when low-resource performance is informative about final performance.
limitations: Successive halving can discard late-blooming configurations when early performance is misleading.
The reduction factor and resource brackets affect the allocation strategy.
